think.script:
Welcome to the Clock Tower!

[ON SCREEN: Tower board]

The Smudge stopped the big clock, and now every train in town is mixed up. The board right under me has six tower jobs. Finish them, and the clock can tell us when the Golem comes.

[ON SCREEN: Two times]

Here's the first puzzle. The tower's log says the clock was stopped for 2 hours 10 minutes. Otto, the clockkeeper, thinks it was 125 minutes. Which time is longer, and by how many minutes?

[ON SCREEN: The big question]

First, wind the clock on your page, so you know how many seconds make a minute and how many minutes make an hour. Then, at the puzzle, look at the two times before you wind anything. What do you notice? What do you wonder? Write that down, then try it your own way. Make a guess and hold on to it. On the Learn tab, the Math Crew will show you two ways.

board.title: Which time is longer, and by how much?

learn.script:
Look at the two times one more time. One has hours and minutes. One has only minutes. We can't compare them until they're written the same way.

[ON SCREEN: Board: The times]

[DRAW: point to Time A's row, 2 | 10. Write 125 min beside the empty row for Time B.]

Time A, 2 hours 10 minutes. Time B, 125 minutes.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Two ways]

[DRAW: fill in Atlas's blanks as you say them, then Felix's.]

Atlas counts full hours in 125: 60, 120. That's 2 hours, with 5 minutes left. 2 hours 5 minutes. Felix changes Time A to minutes. 2 times 60 is 120, plus 10 is 130. 130 minus 125 is 5. Both ways say Time A, by 5 minutes.

Pause here. Say out loud which way is more like what you did.

[ON SCREEN: Live: Restart the Hands]

[DO: tap + 5 s twelve times for one full turn. Tap + 1 full turn six times. Tap + 5 s five times. Type 445 and tap Check.]

The second hand needs 7 minutes 25 seconds. Each full turn is 60 seconds: 7 turns, then 25 more. 7 times 60 is 420, plus 25 is 445 seconds. Remember: time trades 60, not 100.

do.script:
Now watch me solve three. Pause any time.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Problem 1]

[DRAW: under 10 h write 10 × 60 = 600 min. Then + 20 min = 620 min.]

10 hours 20 minutes, all in minutes. Each hour is 60 minutes, so 10 hours is 600. Add the 20: 620 minutes.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Problem 2]

Your turn first. Pause the video and try this one on paper. Then press play and check.

[DRAW: count 60, 120 beside the bond. Write 120 and 35 in the bond. Under 120 write 2 h. Then 2 h 35 min.]

155 minutes, up to hours. I count by 60s: 60, 120. Another 60 would go past 155. So 120 minutes is 2 hours, and 35 minutes are left. 2 hours 35 minutes.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Problem 3]

[DRAW: under h write 2 × 24 = 48. Under min write 48 × 60 = 2,880.]

2 days, down two steps. Days to hours uses 24: 48 hours. Hours to minutes uses 60: 2,880 minutes.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Spot the mistake]

[DRAW: circle 1 h 75 min. Write 175 = 120 + 55, then 2 h 55 min.]

Is this right? Someone treated an hour like 100 minutes. An hour is 60. 175 minutes is two 60s and 55 more: 2 hours 55 minutes. Trade 60, never 100!

parts.label: Two ways
parts.title: Multiply down · count 60s up
parts.body: Hours and minutes trade 60. Days and hours trade 24.

wrap.script:
Look how far you came!

[ON SCREEN: Two ways]

Today you wound the Clock Tower's hands. Going down to a smaller unit, you multiply by 60, or by 24 for days. Going up, you count full groups of 60 and keep the leftover. And the stopped clock? Time A was longer, by 5 minutes.

[ON SCREEN: The timetable]

And the Smudge's timetable? You wound 75 more minutes past 1 hour. 60 of them made another full turn, and 15 were left. 1 hour 75 minutes is really 2 hours 15 minutes.

[ON SCREEN: Next time]

The clock is ticking again. Next time we visit the night market and bring fractions into measurement. See you there, explorers!
